name: What's the difference between an attached and a detached mother-in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between an attached and a detached mother-in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached mother-in-law suite is physically connected to the main house, often sharing a wall or being built as an extension. It might have a separate entrance but is part of the existing structure. A detached suite is a completely separate building on the property, offering maximum privacy and independence. Attached units can sometimes be more cost-effective due to shared utilities or foundations, while detached units provide greater separation and often more flexibility in design. Your choice depends on space, budget, and privacy needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites are connected to the main house, while detached suites are separate buildings. Attached units can be more cost-effective; detached offer greater privacy.
